x: The Sun Prairie Police Department (SNPD) utilizes Automated License Plate Readers (ALPR) to enhance public safety, aid in criminal investigations, and improve law enforcement efficiency. ALPR capture infrared images of vehicle license plates, convert them to digital text using Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technology, and match them against databases of license plates of interest. ALPR can alert officers when a match is detected, aiding in identifying stolen vehicles, wanted persons, and other subjects of interest. To provide department members with guidelines on the proper use of the ALPR in their official duties.

• ALPR (Automated License Plate Reader): A system consisting of cameras and technology that captures images of vehicle license plates, converts them to digital text using OCR, and compares them to databases of vehicles of interest. • OCR (Optical Character Recognition): Technology that identifies printed characters using photoelectric devices and computer software. • Read: A digital image of a license plate and associated metadata (e.g., date, time, and geographic coordinates) captured by the ALPR system. • Alert: A visual and/or auditory notice triggered when an ALPR system detects a match between a scanned license plate

The Chief of Police shall assign a System Administrator who is responsible for overseeing the ALPR program, including the installation, maintenance, and operation of ALPR units. This individual will also manage system security, data retention, and system audits.
ALPR data will be retained for 30 days unless needed for investigative purposes.
q: How long is data kept? (Policy: 30 days unless needed for an investigation.)

x: Only authorized department personnel who have received training in the use of ALPR systems may access or operate the system. Unauthorized access or use of ALPR data is strictly prohibited.
Authorized users must log into the ALPR system using their designated credentials. All access will be automatically logged, including the date, time, user identity, and purpose of access.
The system will automatically record all queries and access to stored ALPR data, including the user, the purpose of the query, and the data retrieved. These logs will be used for auditing purposes.
q: Are searches logged? (Policy: yes, with user and purpose.)

x: ALPR data is confidential and restricted to legitimate law enforcement purposes.
Personnel authorized to access or use ALPR systems must undergo background investigations, including CIB and FBI record checks by fingerprint identification, before being granted access.

Upon receiving an alert, officers must visually verify that the license plate matches the plate read by the ALPR system. Officers must also verify the current status of the vehicle through dispatch or a law enforcement database (e.g., NCIC, TIME) before taking any enforcement action.

Any law enforcement actions taken based on an ALPR alert must be documented in a report or citation, including the reason for the stop, the verification process, and any enforcement actions taken. Standardized statement: "The vehicle was identified via the Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) system. The license plate was visually verified, and the status was confirmed through NCIC/TIME before enforcement action was taken."
Officers are required to report all successful uses of the ALPR system (e.g., identification of stolen vehicles or wanted persons) to the System Administrator by using the ALPR classification in RMS.

Authorized personnel may query stored ALPR data only when there is a reasonable belief that the data relates to an active investigation or legitimate law enforcement objective. Authorized users shall document the purpose of all ALPR searches. At a minimum, documentation for each search shall include: (1) A case number — a Sun Prairie or another agency's case number; if none exists yet, a Sun Prairie case number shall be generated. (2) A search type selected from the ALPR system's standardized incident categories (aligned with crime classifications such as NIBRS). x: ALPR data may be shared through the department-approved license plate reader system with designated law enforcement agencies. ALPR data shall not be shared with federal agencies unless required by court order or expressly approved by the Chief of Police.
q: Who can data be shared with?

x: ALPR data shall only be released to law enforcement agencies for legitimate law enforcement purposes. Any request from non-law enforcement entities must go through the department's open records process. Any other release to non-law enforcement agencies, private individuals, or external organizations is strictly prohibited unless required by court order, subpoena, or the chief or their designee.

The System Administrator shall be responsible for ALPR auditing and audit-related reporting. Audits shall assess compliance with this policy and applicable law, including review of system access, search activity, documentation of search purpose, and adherence to data retention periods. The System Administrator shall compile periodic ALPR usage and audit summary reports, which may include the number of reads, alerts, successful deployments, and any identified policy violations. x: The department will regularly review its ALPR systems. The System Administrator will be responsible for (1) implementing necessary software or hardware updates; (2) ensuring updates comply with current legal and regulatory standards; and (3) regularly evaluating the system for required modifications to ensure performance and continued compliance with privacy laws.

Only authorized personnel with a clear law enforcement purpose may access stored ALPR data. All access is automatically logged and subject to regular audits. Any employee becoming aware of a possible violation, including unauthorized access, use, release and/or dissemination of LPR data, shall refer the matter to his or her supervisor.

ALPR systems are only used for legitimate law enforcement objectives, including locating stolen vehicles, identifying wanted persons, and supporting criminal investigations. The system shall not be used to, nor is designed to, surveil or track individuals or vehicles without reasonable suspicion of a crime.
ALPR technology shall not be used to monitor individuals or groups based on protected characteristics such as race, religion, gender, or political affiliation.

The department will provide annual reports summarizing the use of ALPR systems, including audits. These reports will be made available to the public in accordance with department policies on public records requests.
